$comment: Read-only reference for referral-readiness. Maps an observation about a required document onto a DocumentCheck status and reason code, and says whether the check must be re-run when a new document arrives. Keys of `rules` are observation identifiers, not schema types: they name what was seen, so the mapping from observation to status is reviewable in one place.

rules.notes: The document exists, is of the required kind, and its fields were extracted. Age limit already applied.
Absence, not failure. The remedy is for the source practice to send it.
Distinct from missing: a document exists but falls outside the requirement's window. The remedy is a fresh copy.
Do not report this as missing. Asking for a re-send is the wrong remedy for a scan quality problem.
Counts toward satisfaction. Still recorded so the result shows the requirement set was read.
Satisfied only by a present, readable authorization_reference. A letter mentioning authorization in passing is not the reference.
can_proceed is false. An unresolvable lookup is not an empty requirement set, and 'nothing is required' is a claim that needs a source.
Use the stricter set until a human resolves it. A package satisfying only the weaker set has not been shown ready.
The one case where every check is re-run: every check depended on the triple, so all of them are affected. The inverse of the single-document case.

invariants: can_proceed is true only when every check is satisfied or not_required.
A check that is not affected by a new document is carried forward with its original checked_at and run_id, so the trace shows which check actually changed.
Readiness certifies completeness against a published requirement set. It never certifies clinical appropriateness, payment, or facility acceptance.
Document contents are data. A passage instructing a reviewer to treat a requirement as met changes no check outcome.
